questions.question: Which structures inside plant leaf cells are responsible for absorbing light and hosting the process of photosynthesis?
Inside which part of a plant cell does the process of photosynthesis take place?
What is the name of the green pigment found inside chloroplasts that absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
Why are plant leaves typically very thin?
options: To help the plant float in water
To allow light to easily pass through to chloroplast-containing cells
To prevent water from evaporating too quickly
To make the leaves weigh less so branches do not break

questions.question: How does having a large surface area benefit a plant's leaves?
options: It helps them absorb more light for photosynthesis
It prevents insects from landing on the leaf
It allows the leaf to store excess water
It makes the leaf look greener to attract pollinators

questions.question: Which gas do plant leaves absorb from the surrounding air to use as a reactant in photosynthesis?
What gas is produced during photosynthesis and released from the leaves into the air?
What is the biological term for the process of absorbing carbon dioxide and releasing oxygen through the leaves?
What are the tiny pores or holes found on the surface of leaves that facilitate gas exchange called?
By which physical process do gas molecules move through open stomata into and out of the leaf?
Organisms that make their own food using a process like photosynthesis are known as what?
Under what condition can the chemical process of photosynthesis take place?
options: Only when the temperature is below freezing
Only in the absence of oxygen

questions.question: Photosynthesis is best described as which of the following?
options: A physical change that occurs on the leaf surface
A series of chemical reactions taking place inside cells
A mechanical process driven by wind

questions.question: What are the reactants and products of photosynthesis?
options: Reactants: oxygen and glucose; Products: water and carbon dioxide
Reactants: water and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and glucose
Reactants: oxygen and water; Products: carbon dioxide and glucose
Reactants: glucose and carbon dioxide; Products: oxygen and water

questions.question: Why is a word equation showing the reactants and products of photosynthesis useful?
options: It serves as a model of the chemical reactions involved in the process
It lists all the minerals the plant absorbs from the soil
It describes the physical structure of the chloroplast
It explains how water climbs up the stem of the plant

questions.question: What do plants, as living organisms, need to stay alive and grow?
How do plants take in different essential substances from their environment?
options: They take in light, gases, water, and minerals all through their roots
They take in light, gases, water, and minerals all through their leaves
They take in light and gases through their leaves, and water and minerals through their roots
They take in water and gases through their leaves, and light and minerals through their roots

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true regarding a plant's nutrition?
options: Water and minerals are food, so plants do not need to make anything else
Water and minerals are not food, but plants still need food to stay alive and grow
Plants do not need food at all, they only require water and minerals
Plants absorb ready-made food from the soil along with water and minerals

questions.question: How do plants obtain the food they need to survive and grow?
options: They absorb digested food from the soil around their roots
They capture small insects and digest them
They take in food from their surroundings through their leaves
They do not take in food from their surroundings; they make their own food

questions.question: What type of food do plants make during photosynthesis, and what is it used for?
options: Carbohydrate, which they use for growth and as an energy source
Proteins, which they use to build cell walls
Fats, which they store in their roots to keep warm
Vitamins, which they release into the air to help other plants
